The IBWC 1962 report entitled "Amistad Dam Power Generating Facilities Financial Justification" states that under normal conditions the flow downstream would vary from 2,500 cubic feet per second to 140,000 cubic feet per second with an installed capacity of 80,000 kilowatts. It is assumed that the present proposal is for a similar capacity and that the estimated flows would be the same. In view of the high flows which could occur from the power releases from Amistad, it is suggested that the IBWC, Maverick County Water District and Central Power and Light Company consider the feasibility of coordinating their operations to obtain optimum generation from both hydro plants. It is recognized that constraints involving downstream and Mexican water rights may limit such coordination.
The addition of two hydroelectric units at Amistad and coordinated operations with the Eagle Pass plant operations would utilize the water power resources in the area. It does not appear that the proposed project would adversely affect any existing steam-electric generating facilities.
The opportunity to provide this information is appreciated. Please keep this office informed of the status of the proposed addition and of the environmental impact studies. Please note that this information is furnished at field level and does not necessarily represent the official views of the Federal Power Commission.
Sincerely yours,
Joseph II. Flood
Acting Regional Engineer
